lessons_for_next_section: TARGET.md carries two entry enumerations, not one: T1's three ways in and T6.2's four consumption entries. A skill's worked-entries shape can already show all four while its definition_of_done still asserts three - check the shape and the criterion as a pair, not as agreeing because they share a file.

A shape's schema.description and examples are invisible to the compose-by-name checker, which reads only text/action/why/note/maps_to/cannot/swap_procedure/question/evidence/default/input/output. A worked-example shape sharing an (id, quote) with a builds_on skill has to be named in a sibling instruction row instead, or have its now-redundant quote dropped (legal for origin=proposed).

Adding a newly-formalized skill to builds_on retroactively activates the compose-by-name checker against every quote already shared with that dependency, including rows the edit never touched - re-run the validator immediately after any builds_on addition, not only after the rows meant to change.

Naming a new dependency in a sentence that already named an old one can silently drop the old name if the sentence is rewritten rather than extended - check what a rewritten invariant stopped naming, not only what it started naming.

docs/skill-manifest.json is the source of truth the validator checks builds_on/used_by against in both directions; a compose-by-name fix on four skills is only half done until the manifest's four builds_on arrays and the dependency's own used_by array are edited to match exactly.
